runtimeEvidence.visualInspection:
# Flags browser QA

Final automated result: **41/41 checks passed**, using headless installed Chrome, production app bundled in memory, local mock Plus account, real repository question objects and media.

Scope: all40 flags files decoded successfully in Chromium and all40 filenames matched their neutral question IDs. Actual gameplay interactions covered one question from each tier: flags-200-901, flags-400-901, flags-600-901, flags-800-901, flags-1000-901. Allfive passed pre-reveal generic alt, no answer in visible text/title/ARIA/src, enlarged-view generic alt, and correct answer/alt after reveal.

Layout checks passed at390×844 and320×844 with no document horizontal overflow and object-fit:contain. Ten320px screenshots, before/after for each selected question, were visually inspected. The flags remain legible inside their cards, prompts wrap cleanly, and revealed Arabic answers match the displayed flags. No visual defect requiring an app change was found in this sample. The UI uses its existing rounded media corners. Scrolling is expected for lower scoring controls on this narrow screen.

The five generated flags' own rows in About → sources showed AI disclosure. No browser JavaScript errors or missing local asset responses occurred.

Initial attempt stopped at About because a hash-only route change correctly invoked the live-game leave-confirmation guard. That initial result is preserved in results-initial-harness-navigation-failure.json; the scratch harness now uses a full local document navigation. This was a harness navigation issue, not an app defect.

Limits: this does not claim40 individual full-gameplay visual reviews, offline behavior, measured difficulty, or country/flag historical correctness. Shared source/data/records were not modified. Final machine-readable evidence is results.json and asset-decode.json.
limitations: Only five questions were individually exercised in gameplay, one from each tier; decoding all 40 assets is not 40 full-gameplay reviews.
No offline or service-worker behavior was exercised by this runtime QA.
Local mock Plus testing is not production authentication, billing or entitlement validation.
Difficulty remains an editorial target without player measurement.
